activities.anchor: Folds are the same story in rock
activities.caption: pair each fault family with the stress it records
activities.name: seisFaultMatch

config.prompt: Pair each fault family with its stress direction and its landscape:

pairs.right: extension — the Basin and Range's stretched landscape
compression — the Himalaya and every subduction megathrust
shear — the San Andreas, sides grinding past each other

config.why: The fault family is the stress direction's signature — read the fault, read the force.

activities.caption: call the length of the rupture
activities.name: seisSumatraEst

config.prompt: The 2004 Sumatra–Andaman quake unzipped a stretch of megathrust roughly how long?
config.why: Roughly 1,300 km — about the distance from Paris to Rome, ruptured in minutes.
config.context: a typical urban quake ruptures a patch tens of kilometres long

activities.anchor: a suspended mass that stays still
activities.caption: true or false — how a seismometer works
activities.name: seisSeismoJudge

config.statement: A seismometer works by a suspended mass being dragged along with the moving ground, and the mass's motion is the record.
config.why: False — the mass stays still (inertia) while the ground moves under it; the relative motion between mass and frame is the ground's motion, and that is what gets recorded.

activities.anchor: their speed ranking is the seismologist's clock
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the wave ranking
activities.name: seisWaveCloze

config.text: %%0%%-waves are fastest (6–8 km/s in crust) and pass through solids and liquids; %%1%%-waves run about half as fast and travel only through solids; %%2%% waves travel slowest along the surface but carry the largest amplitudes. The %%3%%-minus-S time lag grows with distance, so three stations triangulate the epicentre.
config.hint: First, second, last — and the lag that does the locating.

activities.anchor: released most of that in a few minutes
activities.caption: drop the marker — the 2004 quake's magnitude
activities.name: seisMagPlace

config.prompt: Where did the 2004 Sumatra quake sit on the magnitude scale?
config.why: M9.1 — each whole step is about 32 times more energy, so it sits tens of thousands of times above a moderate M6.

activities.anchor: The tsunami physics is worth one sentence
activities.caption: rebuild a tsunami — from seafloor to shore
activities.name: seisTsunamiOrder

config.prompt: Rebuild the tsunami sequence — what happens first:
items: A subsea megathrust heaves the seafloor
The water column above follows, raised wholesale
The wave crosses the ocean at jet speed — hundreds of kilometres long, under a metre high
The floor shoals: the wave slows, compresses and rears up
config.why: That is why ships at sea pass through tsunamis unharmed, and coast dwellers must not.

activities.anchor: most seismologists doubt it ever will be
activities.caption: file each practice under the honesty of its claim
activities.name: seisForecastSort

config.prompt: File each practice under what it actually offers:

items.label: "a quake will strike here on this date"
"a 30% chance of M ≥ 6.7 in the Bay Area by 2043"
Oklahoma's quake rate rising 300-fold with wastewater injection
trenching faults to read prehistoric ruptures

config.why: Prediction remains unsolved; forecasting drives the land-use rules and building codes that are the true life-savers; induced seismicity is human-caused, therefore human-manageable.

activities.caption: the rock's head start versus the alert — drag the divider
activities.name: seisWarnCompare

config.prompt: Early warning in one card — drag the divider:

before.label: the rock's warning
before.text: P-waves arrive first — harmless, but fast; the damaging S- and surface waves trail seconds behind

after.label: the electronic alert
after.text: radio outruns both: trains stopped, factory lines cut, phones buzzing before the sway

config.why: Seconds stop trains, surgeries and elevators — and multiplied over millions of people, they are worth as many lives as any building code.

activities.anchor: the field's centre of gravity is the
activities.caption: find the backwards claim — the scaling law
activities.name: seisGRSpot

config.prompt: One of these claims about quake scaling is backwards — click it:
lines: Moment magnitude reports rigidity × rupture area × slip.
Rupture area grows with fault length, so great quakes are disproportionate.
For every whole-number step down in magnitude, quakes are about ten times more frequent.
A quake twice as long releases exactly twice the energy.
config.correction: Rupture area grows quadratically with length — a quake twice as long releases far more than twice the energy.
config.why: That disproportion is why magnitude-9 events are generational while magnitude-3 events are nuisance news.
